s1.syndrome_frame: Gastric mucosal abnormality with autoimmune associations
salient_findings: Red streaks and slight mucosal swelling on the lesser curvature of the gastric corpus
Foveolar hyperplasia and mild degeneration of parietal cells
Mild lymphocytic infiltration and disorganized layer contours
key_facts: Patient has systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjögren’s syndrome
Scheduled for upper gastrointestinal endoscopy before starting prednisolone
Never received acid-secretion inhibitors
Vital signs and physical examination were unremarkable
Endoscopic findings showed normal antrum and gastric corpus with red streaks
Histologic findings showed foveolar hyperplasia and mild degeneration of parietal cells
H+/K+-ATPase staining was heterogeneously reduced
Pepsinogen I staining was uneven
MUC6 was positive throughout the region
Chromogranin A showed slight enterochromaffin-like cell hyperplasia
Anti-parietal cell antibody was negative
Anti-intrinsic factor antibody was negative
Serum gastrin was within normal range
Vitamin B12 was within normal range
Anti-H. pylori IgG was negative

shortlist.label: Autoimmune gastritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has autoimmune associations and histologic findings showed foveolar hyperplasia and mild degeneration of parietal cells

shortlist.label: Chronic atrophic gastritis
shortlist.why_kept: Histologic findings showed mild degeneration of parietal cells and heterogeneously reduced H+/K+-ATPase staining

shortlist.label: Sjögren's syndrome-associated gastritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has Sjögren's syndrome and histologic findings showed mild lymphocytic infiltration

shortlist.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus-associated gastritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has systemic lupus erythematosus and histologic findings showed mild lymphocytic infiltration

shortlist.label: Lymphocytic gastritis
shortlist.why_kept: Histologic findings showed mild lymphocytic infiltration and layer contours slightly disorganized

raw.rationale: The patient has Sjögren's syndrome and the histologic findings of foveolar hyperplasia, mild degeneration of parietal cells, and mild lymphocytic infiltration are consistent with this condition. The negative anti-parietal cell antibody and normal serum gastrin levels also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Autoimmune gastritis
rejected.why: Negative anti-parietal cell antibody and normal serum gastrin levels do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Chronic atrophic gastritis
rejected.why: Histologic findings do not show significant atrophy of the gastric mucosa

rejected.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus-associated gastritis
rejected.why: While the patient has systemic lupus erythematosus, the histologic findings are more consistent with Sjögren's syndrome-associated gastritis

rejected.label: Lymphocytic gastritis
rejected.why: While there is mild lymphocytic infiltration, the other histologic findings are more consistent with Sjögren's syndrome-associated gastritis
